caption: Why a database index sits unused when the query wraps the column in a function, and how an expression index fixes it.

hook.text: Index exists, but the query ignores it?

problem.narration: You have an index on a column. Then your query wraps that column in a function, like lower. The plain index on col1 does not match lower of col1, so the database may read the whole table instead.

fix.narration: The fix is an expression index. An index column need not be just a column of the table. It can be a function computed from one or more columns. Create the index on lower of col1, and this query can use it.

explain.narration: To check, run EXPLAIN before the query. The planner shows its choice. With no WHERE clause, it must scan all the rows, so it picks a sequential scan. Fetching rows by index is cheaper when not all pages have to be visited.

outro.narration: Now you know why the index was skipped. More breakdowns like this on elvaric.
